subject: Post-call: Lumen Health — residency, failover & log retention questions

Subject: Post-call: Lumen Health — residency, failover & log retention questions

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — great to hear more about the Lumen Health use case. Quick recap and a few specific follow-ups you asked us to confirm: 

What we covered (short):
- Primary requirement: patient data (PHI/PII) must remain in EU production and at-rest encrypted.
- Acceptable failover: warm-standby in a secondary EU region; cross-border failover to US only if explicitly authorized and documented.
- Log/metrics retention: need ability to limit PII in logs and set retention to 90 days by default, with archival options.
- Audits & evidence: SOC 2 + DPA requested; procurement will want a copy.

Specific asks from your team for next steps:
1) Confirm pinning granularity — can we pin by tenant or by route (per API key)?
2) Explain failover behavior and how cross-region failover would be triggered and logged.
3) Clarify backups: snapshot cadence, encryption, and where backups are stored.
4) Confirm log retention controls and whether we can redact or pseudonymize request payloads before storage.

I'm attaching a short region FAQ and an SLA digest that answers a few of these already — see attachment stubs below.

Can you confirm whether Lumen requires strictly EU-only encryption key management (KMS/HSM) or if Redwood KMS with EU key residency would be acceptable? Also let me know a couple 1-hour slots for a technical deep-dive with your infra/security team — Karthik will lead that.

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik: technical deep-dive (30–60m) — cover pinning, failover, backups, and log redaction.
- Marissa: procurement intro and DPA/SOC2 delivery.
- I will prepare a short scope doc and sample config for tenant-pin + route examples.

Thanks,

Mina Haddad
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Mina — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline: 

- EU-only production: yes, Lumen requires EU residency for any PHI processing. We can consider controlled failover to the US for non-PII workloads only, but the contract must list permitted scenarios.
- Pinning: tenant-level pinning is required for production traffic; for testing we can accept route-level controls.
- Backups: must be stored in EU; we need details on snapshot frequency and restoration SLAs.
- Logs: procurement will want an option to redact identifiable fields before long-term storage. 90 days default retention is fine.

Procurement has asked for SOC 2 Type II and a DPA draft — I attached our procurement email thread with additional legal points (attached as stub).

Preferred times for the technical deep-dive next week: Tue 2027-03-23 10:00–11:00 CET or Wed 2027-03-24 14:00–15:00 CET. Please confirm.

Best,
Elena Silva

Hi Elena — thanks for the clarifications. A few concrete notes from our side so the deep-dive is focused: 

1) Pinning granularity
- Redwood supports per-tenant pinning (recommended for production). That pins both inference execution and associated ephemeral KV caches to chosen region(s).
- Route/API-key pinning is available for dev/test; production routing should use tenant pins for consistent locality guarantees.

2) Failover semantics
- We support configurable failover policies: warm-standby (automated failover within same region group), geo-failover (to another EU region), and cross-border failover (EU -> US) only on allowlist and only for non-PII routes.
- All failover events are logged with event id, timestamps, and reason; logs include masked request identifiers — payloads are not stored unless explicitly enabled.

3) Backups & snapshots
- Snapshots are taken every 24 hours by default and stored encrypted at rest in the pinned region.
- Optional longer-term archival to cold storage in the same geo is available on request.
- Restore SLA: standard RTO is 4 hours for tenant-level restores; expedited restores available under dedicated capacity contracts.

4) Logging and redaction
- We offer pre-ingest redaction hooks: you can configure field-level redaction or pseudonymization at the ingestion layer.
- Default operational logs retain metadata only for 90 days; customers can request shorter retention windows or export and purge programmatically.

5) Key management
- We support two options: Redwood-managed KMS with keys exclusively stored in the EU, or customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own) integrated via KMIP/KMS APIs.

I'll prepare a short config snippet showing tenant-pin + a sample failover policy and share in the deep-dive. Attached are the region FAQ and a short SLA summary that map to items above.

Proposed deep-dive slots to cover technical config + PK/infra: Tue 2027-03-23 10:00–11:00 CET (works for our infra), or Wed 2027-03-24 14:00–15:00 CET. Which do you prefer?

Thanks,
